channel.title: AI Campaign News (AICN)
channel.description: A tracker of AI use in political campaigns, elections, and advocacy.

item.title: AI Avatar of Jair Bolsonaro Sparks Legal Battle Ahead of Brazil 2026 Presidential Election
item.description: An AI-generated avatar of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro has sparked a legal dispute ahead of Brazil's 2026 presidential election, raising questions about the use of synthetic candidate likenesses in campaign content.

item.title: Sen. Blackburn fights AI-generated attack ad
item.description: Sen. Marsha Blackburn is fighting back against an AI-generated attack ad targeting her in Tennessee.

item.title: Political AI campaigns targeted by California Democrats
item.description: California Sens. Adam Schiff and Ro Khanna are pushing federal legislation to ban AI-generated political ads, prompted in part by viral AI-produced political attacks involving Spencer Pratt and Steve Hilton.

item.title: Adam Schiff attack on free speech is a parody of itself
item.description: A New York Post editorial argues that Sen. Adam Schiff's proposed legislation targeting AI-generated political ads is overbroad, criticizing it for lacking a parody carveout and characterizing it as a free-speech threat.

item.title: AI Regulation in Congress: Every Bill, Vote, and Floor Quote (2026)
item.description: Legisletter maintains a running tracker of AI-related legislation in the 119th Congress, covering deepfake bans, state preemption fights, algorithmic accountability, and data center issues, updated weekly with floor quotes and lobbying filings.

item.title: Exclusive: Senate Democrat's new bills would restrict AI-powered ads and paid influencers
item.description: California Sen. Adam Schiff plans to introduce two bills: one that would restrict AI-generated likenesses of politicians in political ads and another that would require disclosure of paid influencers in political speech online.

item.title: Lawmakers Are Riding the AI Wave to Stardom
item.description: NOTUS reports that politicians who can speak credibly to AI issues are gaining visibility and credibility with voters and within their parties, positioning AI as a political credential in the 2026 cycle.

item.title: 2026 State Legislative Push to Regulate AI-Generated Campaign Advertisements
item.description: Duane Morris Government Strategies surveys 2026 state legislation targeting AI-generated political ads, noting states are introducing bills ranging from mandatory disclosure requirements to outright pre-election bans on synthetic media.

item.title: How One Voter Data Firm is Meeting the AI Age
item.description: Campaigns & Elections profiles L2, a voter data firm, and its cautious approach to integrating AI into its products, contrasting it with faster-moving competitors in the political data space.

item.title: Aaru - Behavior simulation at the scale of the real world.
item.description: Aaru, a behavior simulation company, markets itself as an alternative to traditional surveys by using AI to simulate human behavior at scale, arguing that conventional polling is distorted by memory failure and social pressure.

item.title: This Is Donald Trump’s AI Brain Trust
item.description: Wired profiles the network of advisers and officials shaping U.S. AI policy inside the Trump administration, with a senior administration official describing internal policy debates as involving many competing factions rather than two clear sides.

item.title: Trump Ramps Up Threats Against Iran Despite Pause in Strikes
item.description: President Trump posted a series of AI-generated images on Truth Social alongside threats directed at Iran, including one depicting himself as "Guardian of the World."

item.title: StackAdapt Launches Political Targeting and Measurement Suite to Help Campaigns Optimize Voter Outreach Ahead of the 2026 Midterms
item.description: StackAdapt, which describes itself as an AI advertising and orchestration platform, has launched a political targeting and measurement suite for the U.S. market, combining political audience creation, voter intelligence, campaign measurement, and ad optimization in a single workflow for political advertisers ahead of the 2026 midterms.

item.title: AI Deepfakes Are Official Campaign Strategy. The 2026 Midterms Proved It.
item.description: RoboRhythms reports that AI-generated deepfakes have become an explicit campaign strategy in the 2026 midterms, noting that no federal law prohibits their use in political advertising.

item.title: How 20 States Are Now Regulating Deepfakes—and What It Means for Elections
item.description: GovFacts surveys the patchwork of deepfake laws across states, noting 47 states have passed some form of deepfake legislation since 2019, while Alaska, Missouri, and Ohio have none, with significant variation in how election-related synthetic media is addressed and enforced.

item.title: State AI deepfake laws face first big test in 2026 midterm elections
item.description: The 2026 midterm elections mark the first major real-world test of a wave of state laws passed to regulate AI-generated content in political campaigns, with questions now turning to enforcement and compliance by campaigns and vendors.

item.title: Voters in Colorado battleground 8th District want more AI oversight
item.description: A new poll of voters in Colorado's swing 8th Congressional District finds bipartisan majorities want more regulation of artificial intelligence, regardless of party affiliation.

item.title: Anthropic doubles funding for AI policy fight ahead of elections
item.description: Anthropic is reportedly doubling its funding dedicated to AI policy engagement ahead of the 2026 elections, intensifying its involvement in shaping how AI intersects with electoral politics.

item.title: The AFL - CIO strategy for AI and the midterm elections
item.description: Marketplace reports on the AFL-CIO's strategy for engaging with AI issues as they relate to the 2026 midterm elections, marking organized labor's explicit connection of AI policy to electoral organizing.

item.title: Elizabeth Warren Says Dark Money Groups Linked to Crypto , AI Spending Million to Hand - Pick Congres
item.description: Sen. Elizabeth Warren criticized PAC spending by groups linked to cryptocurrency and AI interests, alleging these groups are spending millions to influence congressional races through dark money.

item.title: Map Shows States Where Governor Candidates Support Data Center Moratoriums
item.description: Newsweek maps gubernatorial candidates in states including Maine, Iowa, Wisconsin, and Kansas who support moratoriums on AI data centers, showing AI infrastructure has become a campaign issue in multiple governor's races.

item.title: Campaigns Need AI Guardrails Before the 2026 Midterms
item.description: A Campaigns & Elections op-ed argues that the political conversation about AI in elections has been too narrowly focused on deepfakes and synthetic media, and calls on campaigns to adopt broader AI guardrails — covering AI-driven targeting, messaging, and voter contact — before the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Tech: Democrats have AI committee hopes too
item.description: Punchbowl News reports that several House Democrats are calling for the creation of a formal bipartisan AI policy committee, mirroring an effort Republicans declined to institutionalize, as Congress continues to grapple with how to organize legislative oversight of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Tech: How Husted and his voters see AI
item.description: Punchbowl News reports that Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) says constituent concern about AI has broadened beyond parents worried about children online to include employers and educators, suggesting AI anxiety is becoming a wider voter issue heading into 2026.

item.title: The Startup Betting on an AI Advertising Tool For Politics
item.description: Campaigns & Elections profiles BattlegroundAI, a startup that has launched an AI tool enabling campaigns to instantly generate platform-compliant programmatic political ads with minimal manual input.

item.title: AI safety group's $15 million GOP play
item.description: Public First Action, an AI safety advocacy group, announced it will spend $15 million in July 2026 to run ads highlighting 16 congressional Republicans for their work on artificial intelligence safety, turning AI policy into an explicit electoral issue.

item.title: AI Moves From Campaign Tool to Campaign Issue
item.description: Governing reports that AI is now reshaping 2026 campaigns on two fronts simultaneously: campaigns are deploying AI operationally, while AI policy itself has emerged as a voter-facing issue candidates must address.

item.title: Tech: Cruz approaches AI's make-or-break month
item.description: Punchbowl News reports that Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz faces a make-or-break window of several weeks to move federal AI legislation forward, with the alternative being a delay until the 120th Congress.

item.title: The First AI Midterms: Early Signals from California
item.description: Higher Ground Labs published a debrief of AI tool use across California's June 2026 primary — covering the governor's race, the Los Angeles mayoral contest, and down-ballot races — framing the cycle as the first major stress test of AI in American electoral politics. The piece draws early operational lessons for campaigns deploying AI in the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Sanders-backed progressives try to make AI the new AIPAC
item.description: Semafor reports that Sanders-aligned progressive organizers are working to build a grassroots political movement opposing AI data center expansion, drawing an explicit parallel to single-issue advocacy campaigns, with New York Gov. Kathy Hochul's data center moratorium cited as evidence the effort is gaining mainstream political traction.
